newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Turkish Cypriots reject new UN document in talks.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Cypriots reject new UN document in talks.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash on Wednesday rejected new, amended U.N. proposals aimed at fostering compromise in Cypriot inter-communal peace talks but will stay at the negotiating table, a senior Turkish official said.

Inal Batu, deputy undersecretary of the Turkish Foreign Ministry who is here representing Turkey as a guarantor state, told Reuters Denktash had refused to discuss or sign the new document tabled on Tuesday at his meeting with Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides and U.N.special Cyprus negotiator Diego Cordovez. "But the negotiations will continue," he said.

Batu said Cordovez had presented his amended proposals despite the objection of Denktash to the tabling of new documents at the five-day talks, held in a hotel in the village of Glion near Montreux and due to end on Saturday.

"The United Nations has submitted a document knowing that the Turkish Cypriot delegation did not come here to negotiate a document. Denktash rejected the document. He has also refused to sign any document," Batu said.

"But Denktash has said he is ready to continue the negotiations," Batu said. He said Denktash reiterated his position at the two-and a-half-hour meeting. Cordovez was due to listen to Clerides at a second meeting scheduled for 1330 GMT.

Batu said Cordovez was pressing the two sides to sign a joint declaration at the talks, aimed at ending the 23-year partition of Cyprus under a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation. But he added: "There will be no joint declaration. If they want to sign a one-sided declaration on their own, they can do it. But there was no need to come to Montreux for that."
